summary: Prompt 2 Phase 2B (diagnostic-session persistence) fully verified: all 14 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_diagnostic_sessions.py pass end-to-end against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (auth guards, session/task/envelope lifecycle, cross-user 404 isolation on GET/PATCH/PUT + list omission, client-supplied user_id/owner ignored, vehicle ownership enforced on create with 404 for another user's vehicle, session/task/transition idempotency with no duplicate audit events, illegal transition -> 409, unknown to_state -> 400, unknown task_type -> 400, terminal state immutable (409 leaving, 200 same-terminal no-op), cancel from any active state, append-only ordered audit trail, full-session restart recovery). Regression suite added at tests/test_regression_with_diag_session.py (4 new tests) confirms /api/vehicles CRUD + /api/scans list + /api/subscription + /api/shop/fleet still work after seeding a diagnostic session with tasks + envelope for the same user (all pass). Full pre-existing suite (74 tests across auth, security, isolation, shop-fleet, subscription, predictions, google-only) also passes — 74/74 + new 4/4 + 14/14 diag-sessions = 92 backend tests green. Frontend Phase 2F /codes screen (web SimulationProvider): banner text is literally 'SIMULATED — preview only, not from a real vehicle' (verified in DOM), every code card renders a SIMULATED provenance chip + UNKNOWN freshness chip, NEVER 'LIVE' or 'MEASURED' anywhere in the DOM, groups render distinctly (CURRENT/PENDING/PERMANENT observed with the simulator's 4 default codes), status filter dropdown present (testID codes-status-filter), tapping a code navigates to /guided-repair?code=P0300&desc=... as required. BLOCKING ISSUE: On web, react-native-web@0.21.0 ships Alert.alert as a NO-OP (verified in node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js -> `static alert() {}`). Consequently, tapping the Clear Codes button (testID=codes-clear) produces NO confirmation dialog, NO post-clear rescan feedback ('Codes Cleared'/'Codes Still Present'/'Clear Failed'), and NO destructive action fires — the Phase 2F clear-flow spec fails on web. This will also silently swallow the read-error alert on web. Fix required: replace Alert.alert calls in /app/frontend/app/codes.tsx (confirmClear, doClear, read) with either a cross-platform custom modal or a Platform.OS === 'web' branch that uses window.confirm + a toast/banner. Real-BLE MEASURED/LIVE path + physical OBD-II Mode 03/04/07 are correctly deferred to a signed native build (documented environment limitation, not tested).

ui_bugs.issue: On web, react-native-web@0.21.0 has `Alert.alert` implemented as a no-op (`class Alert { static alert() {} }` in node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js). Result: tapping [data-testid=codes-clear] neither shows the 'Clear Codes?' confirmation dialog nor invokes doClear(), so no post-clear rescan happens and no success/failure text is ever surfaced. Same class of silent failure applies to the read-error path (Alert.alert('Read Codes', ...)) and to the 'Codes Cleared' / 'Codes Still Present' / 'Clear Failed' toasts. This directly breaks the Phase 2F acceptance criterion 'Clear Codes shows a confirmation dialog mentioning a post-clear rescan; after confirming it runs a rescan and reports remaining codes'. Reference: /app/frontend/app/codes.tsx:125, :131-138, :151-159.

When a code originating from the SIMULATED codes list is tapped, the /guided-repair screen renders a green 'REAL VEHICLE DATA' pill next to the code. This is inconsistent with the spec's truth-labeling boundary: simulated evidence must never be presented as real vehicle data. Not part of the /codes vertical slice per the review scope but visible one hop away and worth fixing while the provenance chain is being wired up. Reference: /app/frontend/app/guided-repair.tsx (label 'REAL VEHICLE DATA').

integration_issues.issue: Because Alert.alert is a no-op on web, the confirmation dialog and the post-clear result banner never render, so the destructive-action UX + rescan reporting cannot be exercised at all on the web SimulationProvider build.

react_native_issues.issue: react-native-web@0.21.0 (package.json) ships a no-op Alert. Anywhere the app relies on Alert.alert with buttons (destructive confirmations, error toasts), the web build silently swallows the interaction. Prefer a cross-platform confirm/modal utility (e.g., a small wrapper that uses Alert.alert on native and a custom View/Modal on web, or window.confirm for yes/no).

State machine rejects illegal transitions with 409, unknown to_state with 400, and treats terminal states as immutable except for same-terminal no-op (200). CANCELLED reachable from any active state. Good.
Envelope records are stamped with the caller's userId server-side; verbatim displayValue/records preserved (no fabrication). Good.

Frontend codes.tsx correctly wires runCodesRead() through the orchestrator, respects mode==='simulation' by never emitting isLiveEvidence=true and forcing Freshness.UNKNOWN + provenance='SIMULATED'. Group headers gate on non-empty status buckets. Good.
codes.tsx `persist()` only fires when v.mode === 'MEASURED' — simulated data is NEVER persisted to /api/diagnostic-sessions. Good.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the Clear Codes miss on web: /app/frontend/node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js exports `class Alert { static alert() {} } export default Alert;` — a deliberate no-op in react-native-web 0.21.0. Because /app/frontend/app/codes.tsx uses `Alert.alert('Clear Codes?', ..., [{text:'Cancel'},{text:'Clear Codes', style:'destructive', onPress: doClear}])` for the destructive confirmation and the same primitive for post-clear result feedback, none of those events reach the user on the web SimulationProvider preview. Native builds (iOS/Android) DO render Alert normally, so this is web-specific. Mitigation: swap to a cross-platform confirm utility (Platform.OS === 'web' -> window.confirm or a Modal, otherwise Alert.alert). No backend change required.
